meaning: The number of camels in the caravan that returned from the Babylonian exile
description: The number 435 appears in the Bible in connection with the census of the people and property that returned to Judah after the Babylonian exile. According to Ezra 2:67 and Nehemiah 7:68, those who returned brought 435 camels with them. This detail is part of the precise census that documented the rebuilding of the Jewish community after the exile, highlighting Scripture's care in preserving historical accuracy. Camels were important pack animals in the ancient Middle East, and their number testifies to the considerable scale of the caravan. Beyond this specific occurrence, the number 435 has no well-established symbolic meaning in biblical or Jewish tradition.

versions.meaning: The number 435 has no well-established symbolic meaning in biblical or Jewish tradition.
versions.description: 435 is not a number highlighted with special symbolism in the Bible or in Jewish numerology (gematria) in any widely recognized way. It may be noted that the Israelites' stay in Egypt is sometimes linked to 430 years (Exodus 12:40), and Paul refers to 430 years in Galatians 3:17, but the number 435 itself has no direct biblical reference. Any numerological interpretations of 435 would be speculative gematria without broad theological recognition.

footnotes.text: The lists in Ezra 2 and Nehemiah 7 are parallel censuses of those who returned from Babylon under Zerubbabel. Minor numerical variations between the two lists occur at several points, but the number of camels (435) is identical in both.
Israel's stay in Egypt is linked to 430 years (Exodus 12:40; Galatians 3:17), a number close to 435, but there is no recognized theological connection between these numbers.
